note: Products for the ChatGPT garment kit (stage 3, WP4). The worker fills this from the shop catalogue and the design reference; the user reviews it. Keyed 'cat:shape' like the garment records. Checked against the live shop for both sexes by `node tools/garment/design-ref.cjs --verify-products` (headless ?demo=1). Used by tools/garment/prompt.cjs.

fields.class: top/short-sleeve | bottom/shorts | shoes/low (stage 3). Other classes exist as schema only. Hats (2026-10-15): hat/full (pulled onto the head, hair above its rim hidden by the game) | hat/sit-on (an ornament seated on the hair). Face decorations (2026-10-15): face/sticker (on the facial skin, front and profile). Face parts (2026-10-15): face/eyes | face/nose | face/mouth (one part changed, front and profile).
fields.sexes: who the shop sells it to (QPGame.getCatalog().curatedItem(cat, shape, sex) is not null). A single-sex product changes only that child; the prompt says the other child stays as it is.
fields.ci: the fixed colour index per sex (index.html CURATED_COLOURS / fixedColour).
fields.colour: the fixed colour: QPGame.getCatalog().curatedItem(cat, shape, sex).color, the palette colour of the colour index (same field name as the garment records' catalog colour).
fields.display: the colour the shop actually paints the garment with: QPClothes.colorFor(cat, shape, sex, colour) || colour, the value avatar-pixel.js writes to data-cloth-color / data-qpx-shoe-color. Equal to colour for girls and shoes; boys' tops and shorts use avatar-clothes.js maleColors (top:shirt m: fixed cream #f2dfbd, painted light blue #82ace1). Compare ChatGPT colours with display: it is what the shop shows and what image 2 carries.
fields.mirrorSafe: true when the right-facing side view may be mirrored into the left view without a decoration looking wrong (no lettering, nothing on one side only that the side view shows). false adds the mirror line to the prompt.
fields.sharedPicture: true when both sexes wear the same painting in the same colour: image 2 shows it once.
fields.designRef: image 2 in assets/garment-template/, made by tools/garment/design-ref.cjs from the shop art (no body).
fields.notes: KO/EN design notes for the prompt. item: the garment noun; look: what to take from image 2; m/f (or both): the description per child; back: the back-view line.
fields.planned: true for a product the shop does not sell yet (requested art first): design-ref.cjs draws image 2 from refSvg and skips the catalogue check.
